title: Subtitle Overlay
description: The SubtitleOverlayPlugin: VTT subtitle rendering, styling, and accessibility (FCC 47 CFR 79.4, WCAG 1.4.4).
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/subtitle-overlay/index.ts / renders the player's webvtt subtitle cue stream as a positioned dom overlay above the video element. register it whenever you serve vtt subtitle tracks. for ass/ssa files use instead, this plugin handles vtt only. plugin id import what it does renders the player's event stream as a positioned dom overlay above the video element. it is a pure consumer, all subtitle parsing, vtt fetching, and cue tracking live in the core. the overlay subscribes to the single event and renders one per active cue. features: - one box per active cue, pooled and reused, no dom churn - webvtt cue layout: , , , and attributes from the vtt cue are applied as css positioning - collision detection, when two cues would overlap, the later one is displaced along the line axis - overlay is letterbox-fit to the actual video display rectangle not the container, so cue font size scales with the visible picture, not the player shell - settings font family, size, color, edge style, background are applied and update live on events - language tag is mirrored onto for css targeting for ass/ssa subtitle files, add the octopusplugin instead, this overlay handles vtt only. options takes no options. all subtitle style settings font family, size, color, edge style, background are driven by the adapter and the api at runtime. registration dom structure the plugin mounts: | element | description | |---------|-------------| | | player root | | | letterbox-fit to the actual video display rectangle | | | 5% top/bottom, 3% left/right inset | | × n | one per active cue, positioned by vtt cue attributes | | | styled by subtitlestyle settings | subtitle style the overlay respects all fields of via : changes are applied immediately to all active cue areas without re-rendering. track selection api the event fires when the active track changes: subtitle cue stream the player emits events as active cues change. this is the low-level cue stream useful for custom renderers: style persistence user style preferences font size, color, background opacity are persisted via the adapter. the default writes to . accessibility the overlay is built around two formal standards, plus a few implementation choices that follow from them. caption placement fcc 47 cfr 79.4 the wrapper insets captions 5% from the top and bottom and 3% from the left and right of the actual video picture, not the player frame. a letterbox-fits that safezone to the real video display rectangle and re-fits on fullscreen changes, so the inset always tracks the picture. pillarboxed 4:3 content gets 3% of the 4:3 picture, not 3% of the wider 16:9 shell. this keeps captions clear of player chrome and device bezels so they stay viewable in their entirety, which is what fcc 47 cfr 79.4 requires, and it matches the placement you see on netflix, youtube, and apple tv+. resizable text wcag 2.1 sc 1.4.4, level aa caption text is sized with . the unit scales with the player's width, so captions grow with the video and follow browser zoom without losing legibility. the value comes from the user's own font-size preference, so anyone who needs bigger text can get it without leaving the player. the 14px floor keeps captions readable even on the smallest players, and the 56px ceiling stops them from swallowing the screen. that satisfies wcag 2.1 sc 1.4.4 resize text: caption text scales well past 200% without losing content. right-to-left text both the cue area and the cue text carry . the browser then applies the unicode bidirectional algorithm to each cue's own content, so arabic, hebrew, and mixed-script subtitles render in the correct direction with no per-language setup. contrast the subtitle style system ships five edge effects drop shadow, uniform outline, depressed, raised, and a stacked shadow that users combine with their own text and background colours. the stacked-shadow preset layers several black shadows into a strong outline that holds up against whatever video sits behind it. the plugin does not compute a fixed contrast ratio for you, because video backgrounds keep changing, but these controls give users what they need to meet wcag 1.4.3 on their own content. screen readers the overlay is visual only. it carries no region and no , so assistive technology does not announce the caption text, and screen reader users are expected to follow the audio track itself. if your app needs on-screen captions announced, add and to the element. see also - octopus plugin ass/ssa - subtitle style store adapter - cycling methods, cyclesubtitles - troubleshooting, subtitles not appearing

title: Octopus (ASS/SSA)
description: OctopusPlugin: libass-based ASS/SSA subtitle rendering via a WASM worker, with auth-gated font loading and graceful degradation.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/octopus/index.ts / octopus ass/ssa is the plugin to reach for when your media library includes anime or any content with styled or subtitle tracks. it wraps the nomercy fork of libass-wasm and handles the lifecycle, font loading, and auth-gating so the wasm worker never touches the network directly. for plain subtitle tracks, use instead. is a plain dependency bundled with the package. the plugin imports it dynamically at runtime as a safety net. when the import fails the plugin logs a warning and marks itself as degraded; playback continues normally and ass/ssa subtitles will not render. plugin id: what it does the plugin listens to the player's event. when a track is selected it resolves the url by calling and indexing into that list by the zero-based index the event carries. if the resolved extension is not or the renderer is torn down and the track is left to the native text-track pipeline or . for ass/ssa files it pre-fetches the subtitle body via the player core's auth pipeline, resolves fonts into blob urls the same way, and instantiates the libass wasm renderer. on the event the renderer is torn down and the per-item font cache is cleared so the new item starts clean. all network i/o goes through the player core auth pipeline. the wasm worker receives pre-fetched content as blob urls and inline strings, it never performs authenticated xhr itself. options | option | type | default | description | | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- | | | | bundled path | url for the modern wasm worker script. | | | | none | url for the legacy non-wasm worker, for browsers without webassembly. | | | | none | font url used when a requested font is not in the item's fonts list. | | | | | static font urls preloaded for every item, supplementing per-item fonts. | | | | library default | renderer target fps. leave unset to let the library choose. | | | | | render quality vs. performance trade-off. | | | | | fetch subtitle chunks lazily, useful for very large ass files. | | | | library default | internal scaler ratio. leave unset for default scaling. | | | | | frames pre-computed ahead of . higher values smooth playback through heavy ass effects at the cost of memory. | | | | | enable debug logging in the libass wasm worker. | events events fire on the plugin channel. subscribe from outside the plugin using the string form. | event | payload | description | | ----- | ------- | ----------- | | | | fired after the libass renderer initialises and the first frame is ready for the given subtitle url. | methods subtitle read or set the active subtitle url directly, bypassing the player core's track list. use this for ass files the consumer supplies outside the array. fonts read or replace the plugin-level static font list. the getter returns blob: urls when fonts have already been fetched and loaded for the active item, or the original plugin-level url strings before the first load. calling it with new urls clears the per-item font cache and re-loads the active subtitle so the new fonts apply immediately. renderer returns the raw libass renderer handle for advanced consumers. the returned value is an opaque object; its type is not part of the public api. the plugin retains lifecycle ownership, do not call on the returned instance directly. font resolution fonts are resolved in this order for each item: 1. the array on the active . each entry is a object whose property is a manifest url or a direct font file url. 2. , static urls registered at plugin level, applied to all items. 3. , a single url used when ass requests a font not found above. all font fetches go through the player core's auth pipeline. each binary is converted to a blob url and passed to the wasm worker. blob urls are revoked when the renderer is torn down to avoid memory leaks. registration see also - subtitleoverlay plugin, vtt subtitle rendering - videoplaylistitem, fonts field - troubleshooting, subtitles not appearing

title: Touch Zones
description: TouchZonesPlugin: mobile tap-to-seek, double-tap controls, and touch-friendly play/pause overlay.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/touch-zones/index.ts / touch zones renders a transparent tap-zone overlay that intercepts touch events before they reach the video element. register it when you expect touch or hybrid pointer/touch input, typically on mobile browsers or touch-screen deployments. it gives you double-tap to seek on the left and right edges, single-tap to toggle controls visibility, and centre double-tap to toggle fullscreen. plugin id import what it does the plugin mounts a css grid overlay at , above the video element but below the desktopui controls overlay at . touch and click events on the zones are intercepted before they reach the video, but control buttons on the desktop-ui layer remain clickable above. layout | column | content | | ----------- | --------------------------------- | | left third | seek backward zone | | centre | play/pause and fullscreen zone | | right third | seek forward zone | on mobile detected via or , two extra zones appear in the centre column: rows 1-2 for volume up and rows 5-6 for volume down. the play/pause zone compresses to rows 3-5 on mobile. tap behaviour | zone | single tap | double tap | | -------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | | left | hide controls only if visible | seek backward | | right | hide controls only if visible | seek forward | | centre desktop | toggle play/pause | toggle fullscreen | | centre mobile | toggle play/pause if controls shown | toggle fullscreen | | volume up mobile | hide controls only if visible | volume up | | volume down mobile | hide controls only if visible | volume down | single-tap on the left and right zones only hides controls; it never shows them. when controls are hidden the container's own touchstart event wakes them, not a zone tap. on desktop non-touch, the centre single-tap always toggles play/pause regardless of controls visibility. seek feedback indicator each seek zone shows a floating circular indicator on double-tap containing a chevron icon and a cumulative label for example after three rapid taps. the indicator collapses around one second after the last tap in a burst. rapid successive taps update the same element rather than stacking new ones. css transitions on and drive the show/hide animation with no javascript animation frames. options | option | type | default | description | | ---------------------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | | | | maximum milliseconds between taps for double-tap detection. | | | | | deprecated. use . when both are set, takes precedence for backwards compatibility. | | | | | seconds to seek on a double-tap. | | | | | when , single-tap on the centre zone never toggles playback. mirror this on if you also use that plugin. | registration register after so the layering is correct. integration with desktopui emits to tell to hide the controls overlay. you do not need to wire this yourself; the two plugins coordinate via the shared event automatically. this plugin only emits the hide direction . the show direction is triggered by the container's own touchstart handler, not by this plugin. if you use on , pass the same option to . both plugins register their own click handlers desktop-ui on the video element, touch-zones on the overlay zones and each needs the switch independently. see also - desktop ui plugin - key handler plugin - tv key handler plugin

title: Skipper
description: Skip intro, recap, and credits segments with optional auto-skip and UI prompts.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/skipper/index.ts / skipper watches the playback position and fires events when the player enters a segment you have tagged as skippable. you wire a "skip intro" button to those events, and when the viewer clicks it, jumps the player past the end of the range. for segments like recaps that nobody wants, set and the plugin seeks without any ui at all. plugin id import what it does the plugin reads from the active playlist item. on every event it checks whether the current position falls inside one of those ranges. if it does, and the kind is not in , it emits so your ui can render a skip button. if the kind is in , it seeks to the range end immediately and emits with . when the player leaves a range by seeking, reaching the end, or the segment being skipped the plugin emits . is one of: options | option | type | default | description | | --------------- | --------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | | | | | segment kinds to skip automatically, no ui shown. | | | | | delay in milliseconds before is emitted after entering a range. | events entered a skippable range. render your skip button. | | | | player left the range or it was skipped. hide the skip button. | | | | a range was jumped. when triggered by . | subscribe from outside the plugin using the string form: methods skippers returns the current playlist item's skippable segments as a flat array of entries. returns when the current item has no data. skip jumps the player past description: DrmPlugin handles EME license acquisition for Widevine, FairPlay, and PlayReady protected streams.

register it when your media requires drm. it probes for eme support at startup, emits and exits cleanly in environments without it jsdom, ssr, and coordinates the key-system handshake when the active once eme is confirmed, the plugin subscribes to the player's event. whenever the active item has a field, it calls again with the item's key system to verify reachability. if that probe fails, it emits . is available for explicit license retrieval. it routes the request through for hmac or proprietary signing and applies / when provided. internally it uses the core's helper, so it inherits the title: Live Transcoding
description: LiveTranscodingPlugin coordinates the player with a server-side transcoder, gating playback until segments are available.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/live-transcoding/index.ts / live transcoding plugin id: is for when your backend encodes video on-demand, segment by segment, and the player needs to know the transcoder's progress before it seeks or starts loading. it opens a websocket to a transcoding control endpoint, and gates and until the server reports that the requested position is already encoded. without a or the plugin is entirely inert: no connections are opened and no gates are applied, so it is safe to register in all configurations. what it does the plugin connects to your server over websocket and listens for job status messages. on it resets progress state and waits for the server to confirm at least position 0 is ready. on it checks whether the seek target is ahead of the transcoder's write head, and if so it waits up to milliseconds before releasing the player. the current write head position is exposed through the method, updated live from server progress messages. options | option | type | default | description | | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- | | | | none | websocket url of the transcoding control endpoint. | | | | none | alias for . either one works; takes priority. | | | | none | polling fallback interval in milliseconds for environments without websocket. | | | | none | seconds of buffer beyond required before resuming after backpressure. | | | | | max milliseconds to wait for the transcoder to reach the seek target before releasing the player. | | | | none | preferred output height hint sent to the encoder. | events | event | payload | description | | ----- | ------- | ----------- | | | | transcoding job accepted by the server. | | | | transcoder write head advanced. seek gate may release. | | | | enough segments available to begin playing. | | | | transcoding error from the server. | | | | transcoding job finished. | server message protocol the plugin reads json messages from the websocket. it recognises these values: | | effect | | ------ | ------ | | | emits and records the . | | | updates the state. emits . releases any pending seek gate if the target is now reachable. | | | emits . | | | emits . | websocket connection errors emit directly, not through a message type. methods transcodedto returns the current transcoder write head in seconds. updated by messages from the server. registration see also - automatic advance - player core, plugin model

description: CastSenderPlugin adds Chromecast sender support to the video player, managing the full CAF session lifecycle and mirroring receiver state back to the local event bus.

title: Tab Leader
description: TabLeaderPlugin uses the Web Locks API to ensure only one tab plays at a time on the same origin.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-kit/src/plugins/tab-leader/index.ts, re-exported verbatim from nomercy-video-player / tab leader solves a specific annoyance: you open your library in two browser tabs and both start playing at once. the plugin uses the browser's web locks api to hold a named lock while a tab is playing. only one tab holds the lock at a time. when a second tab requests it, the browser queues that request and hands the lock over the moment the first tab releases it or closes. reach for this plugin whenever you need to guarantee that only one player instance on the same origin is active at a time. if you want finer control, such as scoping leadership to a single player instance rather than the whole origin, pass a factory in the options. plugin id: what it does on the plugin calls . the browser hands the lock to the first tab that requests it. that tab emits and is free to play. other tabs queue behind it. when the leader tab closes or calls , the browser hands the lock to the next queued tab, which emits in turn. in environments without safari below 15.4 the plugin emits and becomes a no-op. playback is unaffected, it just does not enforce single-tab behaviour. options | option | type | default | description | | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- | | | | | action taken when this tab loses the leader lock. calls . calls so audio stops but buffering continues. | | | | | re-request the lock whenever the tab becomes visible via . set explicitly to to disable; absence is treated as . | | | | | factory returning the lock key. when absent, the plugin falls back to the shared key , which is global across all instances on the same origin. return a per-player or per-session string to scope leadership more narrowly. | events | event | payload | description | | ----- | ------- | ----------- | | | | this tab now holds the lock and is the active player. | | | | lock released voluntarily via or when the plugin disposes. | | | | web locks not available in this environment. the plugin is inert. | methods isleader returns when this tab currently holds the leader lock. requestlock queue a lock-acquire request. the returned promise resolves when the lock is released via , plugin disposal, or tab close, not when it is first acquired. calling while an election is already in progress returns the existing pending promise rather than starting a second one. releaselock voluntarily release the leader lock. emits when this tab was the leader. the next queued tab acquires the lock immediately. no-ops if this tab is not currently the leader. requestleadership / releaseleadership backwards-compatible aliases for and . resolves to when leadership is held after the attempt, otherwise. prefer the non-alias names in new code. registration scoping to a specific player by default the lock key is global to the origin, so one tab plays at a time across all player instances on that origin. pass to scope it to a server id, content item, or session: reading leader state see also - message plugin - embed plugin - player core plugins

migrating from v1, read the v1 to v2 section at the bottom first, because the public export surface changed significantly. what is actually exported in v2 the v2 package exposes a focused, lean public surface. unlike v1, there is no batch of standalone string, time, and colour helpers re-exported from the package root. the utilities that used to live at are now either: - internalised inside the plugin that needs them time formatting inside 's progress bar, colour parsing inside its subtitle-settings menu. - available through the player api, for example reading or writing through rather than hand-building a style object from exported constants. - not ported, because v2 plugin architecture removed the use cases that required them title-casing and episode-title splitting are application-layer concerns that belong in your consumer plugin, not in the player package. subtitle style constants the subtitle-style constants that were exported from v1 , , exist in v2 inside . title: Subtitles
description: VTT default rendering, ASS/SSA via OctopusPlugin with dynamic load, multi-language switching, and style customization.
content: subtitles subtitle rendering beyond the quickstart basics: the two rendering paths vtt and ass/ssa, multi-language switching, and user style preferences. prerequisites: video quick start. for the full subtitle api see subtitle overlay. vtt subtitles, default path renders webvtt cues as styled dom text over the video. it is the lightest option and works without any extra dependencies. switch languages at runtime: listen for changes: ass/ssa subtitles, octopusplugin use when you need full ass/ssa typesetting: custom fonts, karaoke effects, complex positioning, motion. it loads at runtime via a dynamic import. copy worker files to your public directory vite example: register the plugin: ships as a dependency of . the plugin loads it lazily, so if it cannot be resolved at runtime e.g. bundler exclusion, it falls back to no rendering with no error thrown. enable to confirm the fallback path. font manifest format the font manifest is a json array. the plugin fetches each font before first render. use a path relative to your own site for a self-hosted font, or a cdn url. bunny fonts a privacy-friendly google fonts mirror is a good source: multi-language switching with vtt and ass mixed you can mix vtt and ass tracks on the same item. the player selects the renderer based on the field: register both plugins. the correct one activates for each track. subtitle style customization subtitle style preferences font size, color, background opacity are read and written via . changes emit the event and repaints active cues immediately. to persist preferences across sessions, call in a listener and save the result to your own storage, then restore it at startup by passing the saved patch to after . what to read next - subtitle overlay, full api reference for both plugins - recipes: quality selection, pairing subtitle language with audio language selection - advanced: custom adapter, writing a custom subtitle style store backed by indexeddb

title: Chapters
description: VTT chapter source, chapter UI overlay via DesktopUiPlugin, and programmatic chapter seek.
content: chapters named chapters in your video, shown on the seek bar and available for programmatic navigation. chapters are provided per item and loaded by an adapter. prerequisites: video quick start. for the full chapter api see chapters. inline chapter data the simplest approach is to embed chapter data directly in each queue item: reads chapter data automatically and renders chapter markers on the seek bar. no extra configuration is needed. vtt chapter file has no field — was removed in v2. the default reads chapters from the array on each item. parse the vtt on your server or in a loader and supply the result as : a valid webvtt chapters file for reference — parse server-side before passing to the player: chapter events and api programmatic chapter seek jump to a chapter by index or by its start time: custom chapter source load chapters from a database or api instead of a vtt file: what to read next - chapters: full ichaptersource interface and chapter type reference - desktop ui: chapter markers on the seek bar are automatic with desktopuiplugin - recipes: subtitles: combining chapter markers with subtitle tracks

title: Playlist and Queue
description: Queue operations (append, prepend, insert, remove, shuffle, sort), peek next/prev, repeat modes, and automatic advance.
content: playlist and queue queue manipulation beyond the basic call in the quickstart: inserting items mid-stream, a shuffle toggle, peek-ahead for preloading, or custom repeat behaviour. the queue api is identical on video and music players. examples use the music player but every method applies to both. queue basics append, prepend, and insert remove and move jump to a track peek next and previous peek is read-only, it does not change playback: shuffle when shuffle is on, returns the next shuffled item. repeat modes auto-advance respects repeat state: with set, the player restarts the current item when it ends instead of advancing the cursor. automatic advance when the current item ends, the player advances to the next one in the queue automatically. this is built in — there is no plugin to register. disable it in when an external orchestrator cast sync, a nomercy connect socket drives itself, so an item is never advanced twice: sorting the queue use the built-in , or sort the array yourself and set it: for in-place shuffling, use fisher-yates before setting: this is a blunt replacement. the active track is preserved because the player matches by . queue events what to read next - recipes: crossfade and gapless: smooth transitions between queue items - recipes: persistence: save and restore queue position across page loads - music: api methods: full queue method reference

title: HLS
description: HDR-aware ABR, quality level constraints, multi-monitor handling, and how hls.js is wired in.
content: hls the video player uses hls.js for hls playback. the player core's stream adapter wraps hls.js behind the interface. hdr-aware abr is automatic. how hls.js is wired in installs automatically with the player a direct dependency of the player package — nothing extra to install for the npm / bundler path. see installation for the cdn exception. the build output marks as external so it is not inlined into the player's own dist bundle. at runtime the player loads it via a dynamic import on first hls source, so it stays out of your initial bundle until you actually play . on safari / ios, native hls is used and hls.js is never instantiated. for the cdn / iife path no bundler, the iife bundle expects as a global, so load via a separate before the player script. see quick start: cdn embed. adaptive bitrate abr abr is on by default. hls.js selects quality levels automatically based on estimated bandwidth. lock to a specific quality level index into : listen for level changes: hdr-aware abr on sdr displays, the player filters hdr levels out of the abr selection pool. hls.js will not automatically promote to an hdr level when the display cannot render it. display-hdr detection uses . no configuration is required. on hdr-capable displays, all levels are eligible. multi-monitor handling: when a player window moves across displays e.g. from an hdr monitor to an sdr one, the player re-evaluates display capabilities and constrains the abr pool accordingly. the re-evaluation runs on the change event. quality level shape returns : auth on hls segments the player's auth pipeline injects on every hls manifest and segment request. no hls.js config needed, the intercepts requests before they reach hls.js. see core, auth and fetch for the full auth pipeline. stream registration the player ships an hls stream factory and a native stream factory. the stream registry picks the right one based on the url and browser capabilities: - urls → hls stream via hls.js - other urls → native src register additional stream types: custom backend for full control over the element or for non-standard streaming protocols: low-latency hls and custom hls.js config the built-in creates its hls.js instance internally and does not currently expose a hook for custom hls.js config — is off and cannot be toggled through the player config. customizing hls.js settings including ll-hls requires supplying your own backend via that owns its instance and implements . see the video backend adapter for the contract.

content: server-side rendering running the player under next.js, nuxt, astro, or any other framework that server-renders html before sending it to the browser. the player is browser-only, requiring , , , and the web audio api. none of these exist on the server. prerequisites: familiarity with your framework's hydration model. for framework integration basics see vue and react. the core rule never call , , or during server execution. these apis access browser globals immediately. calling them on the server throws or produces reference errors. all player initialization must be deferred to the client, after the first render. next.js app router mark the player component and wrap in a . use it in a server component page, and the boundary handles the split: next.js pages router use import with : nuxt 3 use to prevent server rendering: inside your player component, initialize in : astro astro renders components on the server by default. use a directive: for react: inside the component, initialize in vue or react exactly as shown above. storage on the server the default accesses . on the server, substitute : in practice, should never run on the server if you follow the patterns above, but this guard prevents crashes if it does. hydration mismatch if your framework complains about hydration mismatches for the player container: 1. ensure the server renders a blank no player markup. 2. the player writes to the container after mount, so this is fine. 3. do not pre-render elements with attributes server-side. a blank container element with a fixed size is the correct server-rendered output. what to read next - advanced: multi-instance: managing multiple players after ssr hydration - video: vue integration: vue composable patterns - video: react integration: react hook patterns - advanced: performance: reducing js size for ssr-heavy apps

title: Embedding
description: iframe embed mode, postMessage control protocol, parent-frame key handling, and autoplay-allow directive.
content: embedding embedding the player in an on a third-party page, or controlling an embedded player from the host page. this covers the postmessage protocol for cross-frame communication and browser permission requirements. why iframes embedding a player in an iframe isolates it from the host page's javascript, css, and security context. it is the standard model for embed codes youtube, vimeo, spotify. the player itself does not require iframe embedding, you can drop it directly in any page. the iframe model is for cases where you are distributing an embed to third-party sites that cannot or should not install the sdk. setting up the embed page use , it handles the full postmessage protocol inbound commands, outbound events, origin validation without boilerplate. the manual approach in the example below is what replaces. with embedplugin recommended listens for messages from allowed origins and dispatches them to the player. it forwards player events as messages to the host page. postmessage protocol inbound commands host → embed: | | effect | | ------------ | ------------------------------------ | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | , 0–100 scale | | | | | | | | | | | | | message shape: . outbound events embed → host: message shape: . host page integration all messages between host and iframe use the / protocol defined by and . autoplay and the allow directive browsers block autoplay with audio unless the user has interacted with the page. the attribute on the grants the embedded player the same autoplay permission as the host: without , the player can only autoplay muted. if your use case requires autoplay with sound, the user must interact with the host page first not just the iframe. fullscreen fullscreen requires on the iframe and attribute. when fullscreen is triggered inside the iframe, the element expands to fill the screen, not the iframe. this is browser-correct behavior. origin security always validate in your handler. never use as the target origin for sensitive commands like loading authenticated content: what to read next - advanced: multi-instance, multiple players in one non-iframe page - advanced: distributed playback, syncing across title: Distributed Playback
description: Group listening, tab-leader coordination, clock synchronization, and drift-correction strategies for synchronized multi-client playback.
content: distributed playback synchronized playback across multiple clients: watch parties, group listening, or any scenario where multiple users or devices must play the same content in lockstep. status note: the nomercy player sdk's first-class group listening feature planned for v2.1 is not yet released. this guide covers the architectural patterns you can implement today using existing player core primitives. the v2.1 will replace the manual setup here. the core problem two clients playing the same hls stream independently will drift apart. sources of drift: - network buffering differences one client buffers, the other doesn't - clock skew between devices system clocks are rarely identical - seek latency seeking takes different amounts of time on different hardware - tab visibility and os throttling background tabs get fewer cpu cycles a robust sync system must measure drift continuously and apply small corrections. architecture: leader + followers the simplest distributed playback model is a single leader that broadcasts state, and n followers that apply it: implementing with signalr or websocket wire the player to a realtime channel via the player core's realtime adapter: connect to the sync channel and apply state: drift correction continuous correction without visible seeks: trigger correction on periodic sync ticks from the server every 2–5 seconds is typical. clock synchronization system clocks differ between clients. measure the offset before using server timestamps: tab leader coordination when a single user has the same player open in multiple tabs e.g. they navigated away and opened a new tab, elect a leader so only one tab is "canonical": roadmap: a group-listening plugin a first-class group-listening plugin is roadmapped for v2.1 to replace the manual coordination above. it is not available in the video player yet — build on the manual patterns in this guide for now. they stay valid once the plugin lands. what to read next - advanced: custom plugin, watch-party-lite plugin for same-device sync - advanced: multi-instance, multiple players on one page - core: auth and fetch, securing websocket connections with bearer tokens

title: Performance

content: performance bundle size, memory usage, and long-session stability for long-running apps. covers tree-shaking, subpath imports, memory budgeting, and verifying there are no leaks. bundle size what ships by default | package | core size min+gzip | with all built-in plugins | | ---------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | | ~18 kb | ~32 kb core + all adapters | | | ~28 kb | ~95 kb incl. hls.js, desktopuiplugin, subtitleoverlayplugin | | | ~24 kb | ~60 kb incl. webaudiobackend, lyricsplugin, equalizerplugin | these are rough estimates, and the actual size depends on which plugins you register and how your bundler tree-shakes. tree-shake by importing only what you use named imports let bundlers eliminate unused code: subpath imports for core-level features if you only need the core no video or music library, import from directly: avoid barrel re-exports in your app hls.js split chunk hls.js is the largest dependency in the video player. configure your bundler to split it into a separate chunk so the player core loads immediately and hls.js loads async: tree-shake hit list these patterns prevent effective tree-shaking: | pattern | why it is a problem | fix | | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | import 'package'pkgkey audiographpluginequalizerpluginoffthis.onqueueappendassertnolistenerleakthis.on...player.on...settimeoutsetintervalthis.timeoutthis.intervalqueueappendindexeddbbackendoctopusplugineventemitterpluginarrayarrayeventlistenerassertnolistenerleak and the full test harness - advanced: multi-instance, memory budget multiplies per instance - advanced: server-side rendering, ssr reduces initial js parse time

title: Migrating from Other Players
description: Migration notes from hls.js, video.js, Plyr, and Tone.js to the NoMercy Player SDK, with concept mapping and API translation.
content: migrating from other players switching to the nomercy player sdk from another library. each section maps that library's concepts to the player core's equivalents and highlights the most common translation mistakes. from hls.js direct usage hls.js is a low-level streaming library, it manages the element and hls parsing but provides no player abstraction. the nomercy video player wraps hls.js behind . concept mapping | hls.js | nomercy video player | | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | | | | | | | | implicit — mounts to that element id | | | | | | | | | | | | to re-enable abr | | | | key differences - you do not instantiate hls.js directly. if you need custom hls.js config, use , see hls. - auth header injection is handled by the player core's auth pipeline, remove any hls.js or you had. from video.js video.js is a full-featured player with its own plugin system and ui. concept mapping | video.js | nomercy video player | | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | | | | | | | | / | same | | / | / | | / | same | | | same | | | same | | | | | / | / | | | same | ui components video.js renders ui inside the player container using its own component system. the nomercy equivalent is . to customize the ui, subclass , do not add elements directly to the container outside the plugin. text tracks from plyr plyr is a minimal ui wrapper over the native element. it has no hls support built in, so users typically pair it with hls.js manually. concept mapping | plyr | nomercy video player | | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | | the id is the element id | | / | same | | property | method | | property, 0–1 | method, 0–100 | | property | / / | | | | | | | | | | | | | hls migration if you were wiring hls.js into plyr manually, remove that code. the nomercy player handles hls internally: from tone.js audio / music apps tone.js is a web audio framework for musical synthesis and scheduling. it is not a media player, so it does not handle queue management, hls streaming, or playlist state. the migration target depends on what you used tone.js for. tone.js as an audio effect chain if you used tone.js for an eq or reverb chain applied to a element, use and instead: tone.js for scheduling if you used to schedule playback events, replace it with the player core's event system: key differences - tone.js is synthesis-first. the nomercy music player is a media player, it streams pre-encoded audio and does not synthesize. - tone.js does not handle hls. the nomercy player does. - tone.js must be started by a user gesture. the nomercy player handles the audiocontext unlock internally. what to read next - title: Troubleshooting
description: Common video player issues and solutions.
content: video does not play symptoms: stays or immediately becomes after . causes and fixes: 1. no playlist item. verify was called and the array is non-empty. 2. browser autoplay policy blocked. most browsers block without a user gesture. call inside a click handler, or configure the player with to satisfy the autoplay requirement. 3. cors on the hls manifest. the media server must return on and responses. check the browser network tab for blocked requests. 4. hls not supported. the loads hls.js when native hls is unavailable. if returns some sandboxed environments, playback will fail silently. check the browser console for the hls.js error. subtitles do not appear symptoms: subtitle track is selected but nothing renders on screen. causes and fixes: 1. subtitleoverlayplugin not registered. vtt/sidecar subtitles require the plugin. add it before : 2. ass/ssa file without octopusplugin. the subtitleoverlayplugin handles vtt only. for / files, add the octopusplugin. its renderer ships with the player, so there is nothing extra to install. 3. subtitle url is not reachable. open the field from your in a new browser tab. cors errors in the network tab confirm a server configuration issue. 4. wrong tag. matches against the field on the track. verify the tag e.g. not . quality levels not available symptoms: returns an empty array after . cause: the hls manifest has not been parsed yet when fires. the event fires when the manifest is parsed. subscribe to it instead of polling: audio context not starting web audio plugins symptoms: audiographplugin emits or audio analysis is silent. cause: browsers start in state. the audiographplugin resumes it on the first event, which must occur inside a user gesture. do not call from outside a click/keydown handler. desktopui back button not visible symptoms: the back button in the top bar never appears. cause: the back button only renders when at least one event listener is registered. wire the listener before or after : pip not available symptoms: does nothing. cause: picture-in-picture is only available in chromium-based browsers on desktop and chrome on android. safari uses the proprietary api. firefox does not support the picture-in-picture api on elements at all. drm handshake fails silently symptoms: drmplugin is registered but video fails to play with no event. checks: 1. confirm is set on the drmplugin options. 2. verify the string matches your cdn: widevine is , fairplay is . 3. check the browser console for eme errors. in safari you must also provide a service certificate for fairplay. title: Video Player
description: nomercy-video-player v2, the headless HLS engine with HDR-aware ABR, subtitle rendering, skip markers, Chromecast, and a built-in UI plugin.
content: nomercy-video-player is the headless hls engine that powers video on nomercy tv. video is the hard part of playback: the stream changes bitrate as the network shifts, hdr has to be matched to the display, subtitles come in several formats, and the picture has to keep playing through all of it. this package does that work and hands you plain events and methods to drive it, with no opinion about your ui. the player is headless — no built-in ui. you drive it through typed events and methods and render the ui with plugins. it is built on , the same core that powers the music player. everything that is not specific to video lives down there, the queue, auth, plugins, i18n, and storage, so this package stays small and focused on the hard video parts. what you get - , the core class, generic over your own playlist item type. - , a factory that creates or returns a named player instance. - video adapter ports you can swap when the defaults do not fit: backend, chapter source, thumbnail source, and subtitle style store. - a full set of built-in plugins, from the desktop ui to subtitle overlays, skip markers, and chromecast. - full typescript types for every public method, event, and config option. install installs automatically with the player a direct dependency of the player package — nothing extra to install for the npm / bundler path. see installation for the cdn exception. prefer no build step? the cdn build exposes a global from a single tag, see quick start: cdn embed. npm name: github: nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-video-player quick navigation |
